subject: Tesla Cybercab In Focus
body_text:

Here's the latest in trending:Regulating AI: New York City bans generative AI for students in public ​elementary and middle schools.Ballooning costs: Oracle's (ORCL) Larry Ellison subpoenaed over Veterans Affairs "boondoggle."Beef-price probe: DOJ requests data from retailers including Amazon (AMZN) and Walmart (WMT).

 Good morning! Here's the latest in trending: 

 Regulating AI: New York City bans generative AI for students in public ​elementary and middle schools.

 Ballooning costs: Oracle's ( ORCL ) Larry Ellison subpoenaed over  Veterans Affairs "boondoggle."

 Beef-price probe: DOJ requests data from retailers including Amazon ( AMZN ) and Walmart ( WMT ).


 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 Next catalyst? 
 
 
 
Getty Images 
 
 
Tesla ( TSLA ) is holding an invite-only Cybercab event today in Austin, Texas. Buzz about the event has been building up amid anecdotal reports of Cybercabs spotted in the wild, including a sighting in New York City.  

 What to expect:  The Cybercab, which will be Tesla's first dedicated robotaxi, is a two-seater designed without a steering wheel or pedals. This makes the Cybercab the only other purpose-built robotaxi in the U.S. with the exception of Zoox ( ZOOX ) vehicles. The Cybercab layout uses a single AC three-phase permanent-magnet electric motor mounted at the front, driving the front wheels through a single-speed reduction gear. Reported motor output is 163 kW, or about 219 horsepower. While some reports suggest that riders may be able to request the Cybercab through Tesla's existing Robotaxi app in Austin this week, a broader rollout is not expected for some time. It's unclear what the Cybercab's pricing will be and if there are any commercial fleet deployments planned.

Morgan Stanley sees two scenarios from the Tesla ( TSLA ) event:

 Bull case: "Launch of a fleet of unsupervised Cybercabs across Austin, Houston, and Dallas for paid retail rides. There is no magic number, but we believe the market needs to see more than a handful (~5-10) Cybercabs on the road. If Tesla successfully launches 25-50 Cybercabs across TX in the days/weeks following the launch event, we expect the stock to react favorably."

 Bear case: "Retail demonstrations only, with limited to no deployed fleet in the field for commercial use. This would do little to reinvigorate excitement about Tesla's robotaxi business, and we would expect the stock to fade following the event."

 SA commentary: "I certainly want to see if Elon Musk is showing (or guiding) any numbers on the Cybercab," SA analyst Deep Value Investing wrote this week. "Costs per unit, costs per operating mile, planned rollout, anything like that would be welcome. I'm not holding my breath , though." In July, Tesla disclosed that its unsupervised robotaxis logged more than 380,000 miles across six U.S. cities. "Waymo's ( WAYMO ) 200M autonomous miles make Tesla's 380,000 unsupervised Robotaxi miles look tiny by comparison," Deep Value Investing noted. "At the current pace of the robotaxi deployment, and considering the gap with Waymo, I think it may take many quarters (perhaps years) for Cybercab to be a tailwind to gross margins."  Projected Robotaxi Growth By Company
